BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Scope:** Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter, reviewed against the Wattlebridge playbook

## Points to note before the issue list

1. **The "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim is not authority.** The Seller says its positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams" and "are not intended to be re-opened." We have no prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. Every playbook fallback that needs her approval (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release) is therefore **unavailable**. We should reopen all points that depart from the playbook.
2. **The "market context" preamble is the Seller's advocacy, not evidence.** The quoted ranges (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are unverified. They should not displace our positions.
3. **The Disclosure Letter partly undercuts the Seller's own cover note.** It confirms that:
   - the Bluefen consent is not in hand,
   - Riverlark is not repaid,
   - the bonuses are missing from the funds flow,
   - DD-012 is a supplied internal source only.

   We should rely on these admissions in our mark-up.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 caps liability at 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket, with only the excess above the basket recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5k de minimis. AUD 50k basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping (first-dollar) basis.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's figures are 5x ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250k of genuine loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Also proposes that the limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore 24 months, and confine the limitation expressly to general Warranty Claims.**
- **Reason:** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "all Claims" wording is a hidden override of the other regimes (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general caps and time limits, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24m),
  - a claims period of at least six years,
  - no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Capping them at 20% is not "simplicity."

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an overriding fraud carve-out. This point is non-negotiable.**
- **Reason:** As drafted, the Seller would limit liability for its own fraud. The playbook does not allow anyone to waive this.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** DL 1.1–1.2 disclose the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and keep only the specific disclosures (DL 2–10).**
- **Reason:** General deemed disclosure would quietly qualify every warranty against everything in the data room.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 bars any claim on matters known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete Cl 8.3.**
  - If any qualifier survives, limit it to the actual knowledge of named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry.
  - It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reason:** As drafted, it undoes our indemnities for matters we have already flagged (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) and stacks on top of the general disclosure.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied once Bluefen delivers its written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
  - Make an effective Bluefen consent, with its 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, a Completion condition.
  - Require obligations stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. DL 2 admits that neither the consent nor the evidence on conditions exists yet.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be dealt with by a release provided after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter,
  - direct repayment from Completion funds,
  - effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-completion release.** Require a payout letter, direct repayment in the funds flow, and executed discharges delivered at Completion.
- **Reason:** A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval. We have neither. DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge has been provided.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and so on), either as a specific funds-flow deduction or seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add a specific funds-flow line item covering the bonuses and on-costs, backed by an indemnity.
- **Reason:** The bonuses fall due at Completion. Unless they are itemised, the Company (and therefore we) pays them. DL 5 admits they are excluded and that the on-cost position is unclear.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering all loss from any defect in ownership or transfer of the Ironquay materials, while keeping the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted.**
  - Broaden Cl 11.1 to cover IP ownership and transfer loss.
  - Keep the cure mechanism: payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment.
- **Reason:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer conditional on cleared payment. There is no receipt or assignment on file, and the AUD 180k figure is unverified in both directions.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - logs preserved,
  - a continuing investigation,
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion,
  - an appropriate specific protection.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the Seller's characterisation.** Add pre-Completion covenants for log preservation, investigation and Buyer updates, and a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** DL 6 confirms that access, scope and notification duty for about 1,240 records are all unresolved. We should not assume a breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, and nor should the Seller assume immateriality.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of each renewal's timing, terminability, accrual and ordinary-course status. No automatic classification either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reserve the position.** Request DD-008 and DD-011 detail and a warranty on their ordinary-course status. Do not yet treat them as Debt or as a price deduction.
- **Reason:** DL 8 is silent on whether the renewals are unavoidable or accrued. The facts are needed before classification.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3 and 13 ("all Claims"), Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 ("all Claims of any nature"), and the title and tax/IP positions all fold every category into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with no general override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Draft each regime separately, and state expressly that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" default would silently cap the indemnities and covenants.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 alone.** Require:
  - ASIC searches,
  - a PPSR search,
  - share certificates,
  - board and shareholder approvals,
  - encumbrance confirmations, including the Riverlark security.
- **Reason:** DL 10 itself concedes that DD-012 is the Seller's source and is not Buyer verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Treats tax and IP as "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Both kept OPEN and separately negotiated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Mark tax and IP as open and outside the general regime.
- **Reason:** Neither point has been resolved. Accepting the Seller's framing would apply the 20% cap and 18-month limit to them by default. (We are not assuming unlimited liability on these points either.)

---

## Suggested next steps

1. **Cover note to Seller counsel.** State that none of the Seller's positions is accepted as agreed, and that no principal-level authority exists on our side for this draft.
2. **Internal flag to Amelia Frost.** Tell her that the Seller is asserting she agreed the fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months, Riverlark release) and confirm that she did not.
3. **Mark-up priorities:**
   1. Fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005)
   2. Fundamental/Title regime (SPA-N-004)
   3. Category separation (SPA-N-014)
   4. Bluefen and Riverlark Completion mechanics (SPA-N-008 and SPA-N-009)
   5. Bonus line item (SPA-N-010)

   Then the economic terms: cap, thresholds and time limit.
